wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the entry points are in-process Go handlers; a panic aborts the test process rather than returning a client error, so a crash cannot score
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: every tested operation decides on the exact source row's project; there is no proxy resource whose ownership could substitute for it (sf_wrong_object.patch in checks/ was verified locally)
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the surfaces have no role or direction variants; every refusal is the same project-scope decision
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the source checks have no adjustment step between identifier and decision; the write-ordering variant (sf_check_after_write.patch) was verified locally and is kept in checks/
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the project identity comes from the authenticated key and the request path and is always present; there is no optional caller-supplied identity form to malform
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision compares the fetched row's project with the caller's project; both are always present (sf_self_compare.patch was verified locally)
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the reference threads the one shared lookup and the subscription handlers; the GET-only variant (sf_get_only.patch) was verified locally and is kept in checks/

traps.shape: project-scoped source read by identifier ignores the project argument
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The published report leads here and the unused project argument makes the intended scope visible.
traps.realistic_because: real advisory route in unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: source write scoped by identifier only, so a caller holding the row can move or overwrite it across projects
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The HTTP handler reads the source first and reports a foreign id as not found, so once the read is scoped the write looks unreachable; the sibling delete query is already project-scoped.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the project-scoped DeleteSource beside it shows the intended pattern

traps.shape: source ownership check nested under endpoint_id and only for incoming projects
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The guard sits in plain sight at the top of the method; it is skipped whenever the update omits the endpoint.

traps.shape: source ownership checked only for incoming projects, while the identifier is persisted for every project type
traps.reason_to_dismiss: source_id reads as an incoming-project field, so a reviewer assumes it is unused for outgoing projects rather than stored and returned.

traps.shape: subscription-to-source join (by identifier and paged list) not constrained by the subscription's project
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The subscription row itself is fetched with its project id, so the response looks project-scoped and the source looks like display metadata.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the read path must also cover rows already stored

traps.shape: coupled must-keep-working value: the public capability lookup by mask identifier has no project and must stay project-agnostic
traps.reason_to_dismiss: An over-broad fix applies the new project rule to the shared mapper or every lookup, breaking the public ingestion capability.
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: coupled must-keep-working value, guarded by the functional suite
